Diagnoses: Generalized anxiety disorder, Autism spectrum disorder.

Functional history (from patient and family):
Communicates needs such as hunger or pain without difficulty. Acts on impulses constantly, including spending all savings in one day and walking out of work mid-shift. Starts tasks independently. Needs simple instructions repeated once or twice. Recognizes scams and is not easily taken advantage of. Cannot work out what to do about even simple problems, such as a burnt-out light bulb. Reality testing intact. Has occasionally left the stove on without noticing.

Diagnoses: ADHD.

Functional history (from patient and family):
Cannot interpret facial expressions or gestures at all. Emotional reactions are sometimes out of proportion. Does not communicate hunger, thirst or pain; caregivers have to anticipate all basic needs. Goes out alone to familiar places only and avoids busy areas. Any change to the daily routine leads to a shutdown lasting hours; family must plan every day in advance. Notices everyday problems readily. Cannot retain a two-step instruction even when it is repeated. Loses focus on simple tasks after 10-15 minutes. Cannot work out what to do about even simple problems, such as a burnt-out light bulb. Takes in and recalls new information well.

Diagnoses: Major depressive disorder.

Functional history (from patient and family):
Has occasionally left the stove on without noticing. Needs new information repeated a few times before it is retained. Will not wash or change clothes unless a caregiver assists every day. Holds a fixed belief that neighbours are controlling their thoughts. Sometimes misses non-verbal cues. Mood swings occasionally lead to risky behaviour such as reckless driving. Gets unsettled when routines change but settles with some reassurance.

Diagnoses: Major depressive disorder, Autism spectrum disorder.

Functional history (from patient and family):
Cannot work out what to do about even simple problems, such as a burnt-out light bulb. Cannot stay on a simple task such as folding laundry for more than a minute or two. Has repeatedly given money to strangers and does not recognize when being exploited. Occasionally interrupts others and makes impulsive purchases. Behaviour appropriate in all settings.

Diagnoses: PTSD, Major depressive disorder.

Functional history (from patient and family):
Needs simple instructions repeated once or twice. Cannot recall what was said a few minutes earlier, even after repetition. Mood stable with no safety concerns. Sometimes does not notice problems such as an overdue bill until reminded. Starts tasks independently. Forgets important events such as a family death and has to be told again. Needs reminders to shower most days. Needs complex spoken information simplified.

Diagnoses: Generalized anxiety disorder, Major depressive disorder.

Diagnoses: Generalized anxiety disorder, Bipolar I disorder.

Functional history (from patient and family):

Sometimes underdresses in cold weather. Sometimes does not mention pain unless asked directly. Shows good awareness of safety risks.

Diagnoses: ADHD.

Functional history (from patient and family):
Cannot make or follow even a simple plan for the day without step-by-step direction. Cannot retain a two-step instruction even when it is repeated. Gets unsettled when routines change but settles with some reassurance. Manages household chores independently. No problems with impulsivity. Cannot work out what to do about even simple problems, such as a burnt-out light bulb. Has not left the house without a family member in over a year because of anxiety. Does not recognize problems such as a flooded kitchen or an empty fridge. Sometimes misses non-verbal cues. Needs help weighing treatment options but can decide with support.

Diagnoses: Generalized anxiety disorder, Major depressive disorder.
